guide.pageSubtitle: Full documentation on how to create and manage news-monitoring bots. Each section is navigable from the menu on the left.
guide.footer: If something isn't clear, skip it and try in the UI. Bot Crawler is forgiving: you can clear everything with one click and try again.

overview.title: What is Bot Crawler
overview.p1: Bot Crawler is a tool for automatically monitoring news sites by keywords. You create a bot with a topic (e.g. 'Pensions in Bulgaria'), give it sources (RSS feeds or HTML pages) and keyword filters. On a schedule you choose, the bot crawls the sources, finds articles matching the keywords and shows them to you in the admin panel.
overview.p2: The goal is to save hours of manual browsing — instead of you cycling through 24chasa, NOI, btv, etc., the bot does it and hands you a ready list of relevant articles. Click 'Start article' → a new article form opens pre-filled from the finding.
overview.callout: Bot Crawler does NOT publish automatically. It is an editorial pre-filtering tool. The final article is written by you, through the usual flow.

create.title: Creating a bot
create.intro: Steps to create a new bot:
steps: Give it a descriptive name (e.g. 'Pensions and social')
Description (optional) — for your convenience and future AI scoring
Pick a schedule — how many minutes/hours/days between runs. Default: hourly.
Add keywords — press Enter after each. 5-15 is recommended.
How far back to look — older articles are skipped
Save → the bot appears in the list with status 'Active'
create.tip: After creation the bot is empty — you need to add at least 1 source (Sources tab) before the first run.

sources.title: Adding a source
sources.intro: A source is a URL where the bot reads articles. 3 types:

rss.title: RSS
rss.body: Machine-readable format. Fast, reliable, but usually contains only the last ~24-48 hours. Example: https://www.24chasa.bg/rss/bulgaria

html.title: HTML
html.body: A regular web page. The bot scrapes it with CSS selectors. Supports pagination (page=2, page=3, etc.). Ideal for search pages and historical extraction.

auto.title: Auto
auto.body: Default — the bot decides. If the URL is RSS, uses RSS. If HTML, scrapes it. If you set maxPages > 1 → forces HTML for pagination.

sources.warning: After 'Test' always check the sample articles — if nothing is found, go to 'Advanced → Selectors' and check/fix the CSS selectors.

selectors.title: CSS selectors (for HTML)
selectors.intro: Selectors tell the bot WHERE in the HTML page the articles are. Standard CSS syntax + @attr suffix for attributes:

rows.note: Link — href attribute of the first <a>
Image — src attribute of the first

selectors.tip: When adding a source and clicking 'Test', auto-detection suggests pre-filled selectors when possible. You can keep them as-is or refine them.

pagination.title: Pagination (Max pages)
pagination.p1: For HTML sources, 'Max pages' controls how many pagination pages the bot crawls each run. Default = 1 (first page only). With 10, it'll crawl /page/1, /page/2, ..., /page/10 (or ?page=1..10).
pagination.p2: When to use: when you want HISTORICAL data (e.g. all 'pensions' articles from the last month, not just today's). The bot stops early if all items are already seen or all are older than 'How far back to look'.
pagination.warning: RSS feeds do NOT support pagination — they have a fixed ~10-50 most recent items. For historical depth, use an HTML source with a search URL.

lookback.title: How far back to look
lookback.p1: Lookback limits how old articles the bot accepts. E.g. 'Last 3 days' skips anything older than 3 days (by publish date). 'Unlimited' accepts everything.
lookback.p2: Useful for fresh news — you don't want a 'pensions' bot pulling 2018 articles from a blog archive. Older articles auto-dismiss on find.

cleanup.title: Findings cleanup
cleanup.intro: Bot Crawler stores every article found. Over time the DB grows. Cleanup controls the size:
cleanup.autoBody: In bot Edit → 'Auto cleanup of findings' section. Configure: day of week, hour, how many oldest findings to delete each run. Default: daily at 03:00 EEST, 100 oldest deleted.
cleanup.autoExample: Example: you have 320 findings. At 03:00 the bot deletes the 100 oldest → 220 remain. Next day if you have 320 again → delete 100 → 220. Stable window.
cleanup.manualBody: In Settings tab → 'Cleanup findings' section — 3 buttons:
manualList: Clear all dismissed — deletes every finding with status 'dismissed'
Clear used older than X months — deletes 'used' findings older than X months
Clear everything (Clear findings) — full wipe; useful when you change keywords and want re-evaluation

bulk.title: Bulk operations on findings
bulk.intro: When you have 200+ findings, manually marking each takes time. Bulk select solves this:
steps: In 'Findings' → check the checkbox of each card you want
Or click 'Select all on this page' (checks the visible 20)
A dark toolbar appears at the top with the selected count
Click 'Reviewed' / 'Dismiss' / 'Used' → all selected get marked at once
bulk.tip: Selection clears automatically on filter / page / sort change — so you don't accidentally mark articles you can't see.

emails.title: Email notifications
emails.p1: After every bot run (manual or scheduled), the system sends a summary email: status, seen / new articles, top 5 findings with thumbnail + link.
emails.p2: Recipients are configured in bot Edit → 'Email notifications' section. Chip-input style: type email → Enter → it becomes a chip. Multiple addresses OK (CC all). Leave empty to use the system defaults (env: CRAWLER_DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_EMAILS).
emails.callout: Emails are sent on EVERY run, not only when there are new findings. If that's too noisy, change the schedule (every 6h instead of every 1h) — a digest option will be added later.

fromFinding.title: Starting an article from a finding
fromFinding.intro: The most useful feature — turns a finding into a ready article form with 2 clicks:
steps: In 'Findings' → find an interesting one → click 'Start article'
The usual new-article form opens with title, description, main image and useful link pre-filled
A yellow banner on top shows the source + an 'Open original' button
Write your OWN content (do NOT copy the original!) → save
fromFinding.warning: IMPORTANT: The pre-fill is a starting point, not a final. Always read the original and write your own content — to avoid plagiarism. The title is a suggestion too, not mandatory.

items.q: Why can't I find articles older than 1-2 days?
items.a:
Because most RSS feeds contain only the last ~24-48 hours.
For historical articles: add an HTML source (e.g. /search?q=pensions) with maxPages = 10+.
Check the source type is 'HTML' or 'Auto' with maxPages > 1.

Auto-scraper didn't recognise the page structure.
Fix: edit the source → Advanced → Selectors (custom) → manually fill the CSS selectors (item, title, link).
Use browser DevTools (F12 → Elements) to find the right selectors.

1. Check bot settings → email recipients or ENV fallback present?
2. Check spam folder.
3. See server logs (docker compose logs server | grep CrawlerEmail).
4. If you see 'SDK_NOT_INSTALLED' or similar — tell the developer.

items.q: How do I add a new admin to the email recipients?
items.a:
Edit the bot → 'Email notifications' → add the email as a chip → Save.
Or update ENV: CRAWLER_DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_EMAILS=email1@..,email2@.. (for all bots).

items.q: Why do some findings have no date (shows 'Found on X')?
items.a:
Because the original page doesn't expose a machine-readable date (<time datetime>) or doesn't expose one at all.
UI shows 'Found on' (foundAt) as a fallback, italic + grey — so you know it's approximate, not exact.

items.q: How do I change keywords without losing old findings?
items.a:
Just edit the bot, change keywords, Save. Old findings stay as they are.
If you want to re-evaluate OLD findings with the new keywords → after the edit, click 'Clear findings' → the next run will find them again and apply the new criteria.

Recommendation: 3-7 sources per topic. More than 10 starts slowing down runs and generating noise.
If you have many topics — make separate bots, don't overload one.

help.name: Short label you'll see in the bots list.
help.description: Free text describing the topic — for your reference and future AI scoring.
help.schedule: How often the bot polls its sources for new articles. Your choice below converts to the technical 'cron' string automatically.
help.cron: Cron is a standard schedule format: minute hour day_of_month month day_of_week. Example: '0 9 * * 1-5' = weekday mornings at 9:00.
help.keywords: The bot will keep an article when its title or description contains at least one (or all — see below) of these words.
help.match: 'Any' = if at least one keyword is present → keep. 'All' = every keyword must be present.
help.caseSensitive: When off (recommended), 'NOI' and 'noi' are treated as the same word.
help.status: Active — runs on schedule. Paused — temporarily off but history kept. Archived — hidden from the main list.
help.useLlm: AI will score each finding's relevance to your topic (0-100). Detailed settings (model, prompt, score threshold, daily cost cap) are in the 'AI' tab.
help.lookBackDays: Skip articles older than the selected window (using their RSS publish date). Useful for fresh news only. 'Unlimited' accepts everything.
help.cleanupEnabled: When enabled, the N oldest findings of this bot are deleted automatically on the chosen day + hour — regardless of status. Disable if you prefer to clean only manually with the buttons below.
help.cleanupDay: Which day of the week the auto-cleanup runs. 'Daily' = every night.
help.cleanupHour: At which hour (Sofia time) the cleanup runs. Recommended at night (02:00-05:00) when traffic is lowest.
help.cleanupBatchSize: How many oldest findings to delete on each run. Example: 100 = from 320 findings → 220 remain (the 100 oldest by foundAt are deleted).
help.notificationEmails: Email addresses to receive a report after every run of this bot. Press Enter (or comma) after each address. Leave empty to use the system defaults.

bot.cleanupSummary: Auto cleanup: {{day}} at {{time}} EEST → {{count}} oldest findings will be deleted.

notifications.fallbackHint: System default emails will be used (CRAWLER_DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_EMAILS).

help.maxPages: For HTML sources: how many pagination pages to crawl (1 = first page only). The bot stops early if all items are already seen or older than the bot's 'How far back' setting. Useful for fetching historical results from search pages (e.g., /search?q=topic&page=1..10).

selectors.title: CSS selectors for HTML
selectors.help: Selectors tell the bot where articles live on the page. Example: 'article.news' picks every element with class news. Attributes use @, e.g. 'a@href' = the href attribute of the first link.
selectors.autoDetectedHint: These values were auto-detected from the page. You can keep them, refine them, or write your own — then click "Re-test".

card.foundAtTooltip: Source doesn't expose a machine-readable publish date — showing when the bot first saw the article.

deleteBot.title: Delete bot
deleteBot.message: Are you sure you want to delete "{{name}}"? This cannot be undone.

deleteSource.title: Delete source
deleteSource.message: Are you sure you want to delete source "{{name}}"?

clearFindings.title: Clear findings
clearFindings.help: Removes all findings for this bot. Useful when you change keywords and want the bot to re-evaluate everything from scratch on the next run.
clearFindings.message: Are you sure you want to delete ALL findings for this bot? They will be re-evaluated on the next run.

master.label: Enable AI scoring with Claude
master.desc: When enabled, every new finding is sent to Claude for a 0-100 relevance score against the bot's topic. Below the threshold → auto-dismissed (if auto-dismiss is on). Per-bot only — doesn't affect other bots.

test.title: Test before enabling
test.desc: Send one article through AI with current settings. See exact prompt + response. Counts toward daily cost cap.

placeholder.extraInstructions: e.g. Ignore foreign-country articles unless about pensions. Score articles with concrete numbers higher.

help.minScore: Articles with a lower AI score → auto-dismissed (if the toggle below is on).
help.autoDismiss: When off: all articles stay as 'new', just get a score badge — you decide manually.
help.temperature: 0 = strict and stable (same input = same score). Higher = more varied scores.
help.maxTokens: Max tokens Claude can return. 300 is enough for score + 1-2 sentences of reasoning.
help.dailyCostCap: When reached, AI scoring stops for the day. New findings are saved without a score, nothing crashes. Resets at Sofia midnight.
help.systemPrompt: Core instructions sent every time. You can use {{bot_description}}, {{keywords}}, {{bot_name}} placeholders. Empty = use built-in default.
help.extraInstructions: Extra instructions appended to the system prompt. Add topic-specific tweaks here.

zone.title: Cleanup findings
zone.desc: Manual bulk operations. Auto-cleanup is configured in Edit → Auto cleanup of findings.

used.help: Deletes findings marked as 'Used' that are older than X months — to free space after long-running work.
